newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen continuing weaker at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen continuing weaker at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks were expected to continue lower after a weak session dominated by a few big plays on Tuesday. * Traders said market would be volatile ahead of triple-witching Friday.
Toronto stocks were expected to follow world markets lower at the open on Wednesday after a weak session dominated by a few big stories yesterday.

"If you look around the world this morning, the world is a weaker place to live in...I just think that you're going to see them go a little weaker, there's not much in the way of economic news today," one trader said.

Volatility will continue to plague the market ahead of triple-witching on Friday, when options, futures and options on futures all expire, the trader said. He said the expiries' influence was clearly seen on Tuesday.
"You saw it yesterday, down 60 points, up 30 points, and close down 11. That's going to continue...the closer we get to Friday, the more influence it has," he said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slipped 5.13 points on Tuesday to close at 6532.34.
The market was dominated by a few big plays.
Shares in key conglomerate Canadian Pacific Ltd jumped in heavy trading after news it sold a stake in Laidlaw Inc worth C$1 billion (US$722 million).
Canadian Pacific owned 47 percent of the transportation and waste management company's class A shares and 11 percent of its class B shares.
Laidlaw's A and B shares also rose on the announcement.
In economic news, Canada's wholesale trade rose 3.0 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in April from March to C$23.22 billion, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 1.2 percent month-on-month rise in April.
StatsCan also revised its figure for March sales to C$22.54 billion from C$22.46 billion.
Canadian manufacturers' shipments rose 0.7 percent in April, to C$35.47 billion seasonally adjusted from a revised C$35.20 billion (C$35.35 billion) in March.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd said overnight it agreed to acquire CS Resources Ltd for C$16 per share plus the assumption of C$56 million in debt, for a total purchase price of C$521 million. The board of directors of both companies approved the deal.
